Name: LEO Platforms
Short description: Orbiting factories and labs.
Extended description: Commercial platforms in low Earth orbit. Crews rotate every few weeks. Earth jurisdiction usually applies via the operator flag state.

Name: Orbital Hotels
Short description: Space tourism, mostly transient.
Extended description: Short-stay platforms hosting paying visitors. Multi-jurisdictional clientele, well-connected to Earth, but services expensive and supply chains thin.

Name: Earth Spaceports
Short description: Launch and customs hubs at the edge of everywhere.
Extended description: Ground-based facilities with freeport status. Border-crossing logic dominates.

Name: Lunar Bases
Short description: First permanent off-Earth settlements.
Extended description: Government and commercial habitats on the Moon. 1.3-second comms lag. Property rights unsettled.

Name: Lunar Mining Camps
Short description: Temporary work sites for resource extraction.
Extended description: Crews on rotation. Migrant labor logic. Contracts run weeks to months.

Name: Lagrange Stations
Short description: Gravitational parking spots between Earth and Moon.
Extended description: Fixed positions where gravity balances. Real-time comms but logistically isolated.
Facilitator notes: Some audiences need the extended description.

Name: Cislunar Cyclers
Short description: Ships looping between Earth and Moon on permanent orbits.
Extended description: Crewed vessels swinging past Earth and Moon every two weeks.

Name: Mars Settlements
Short description: Months from Earth, building local economy.
Extended description: 4-24 minute comms lag. Local rules emerge because Earth is too slow to enforce them.

Name: Asteroid Claims
Short description: Rights to mine a moving rock.
Extended description: Ownership contested. May not return to convenient orbit for years.

Name: Ceres Station
Short description: Belt trading hub.
Extended description: Largest object in the asteroid belt. Multiple operators co-located.

Name: Europa Outposts
Short description: Under Jovian ice, hours of comms blackout.
Extended description: Jupiter blocks comms on a predictable schedule. Radiation is high.

Name: Earth-Mars Cyclers
Short description: Permanent transit infrastructure between two worlds.
Extended description: Vessels in continuous orbit. Crews live on board for years.

Name: Titan Refineries
Short description: Fuel processing in the outer system.
Extended description: Cold, slow and isolated, but rich in hydrocarbons for outbound vessels.

Name: Generation Ships
Short description: Journeys lasting decades; born on board, die on board.
Extended description: Self-contained vessels. Multiple generations. Internal economy must be fully self-sustaining.
Facilitator notes: Highly speculative. Anchor to near-term cards if pushback.

Name: Comet Claims
Short description: Objects passing through every few decades.
Extended description: Long-period comets. Returns measured in human lifetimes.

Name: Probe Investments
Short description: Returns come after the investor is dead.
Extended description: Robotic missions. Payoff returns decades later to whoever inherited the contract.

Latency: Days to over a year each way
Name: Oort Stations
Short description: Years from anywhere, at the edge of the system.
Extended description: Round-trip comms measured in years. Communities tiny and tightly bound.

Name: Relativistic Vessels
Short description: Ships moving fast enough that time dilates.
Extended description: Contracts must address whose clock counts.
Facilitator notes: Strong with physics-comfortable audiences only.

Name: Orbital Service Depot
Short description: A pit stop in orbit for assets that cannot come home.
Extended description: In-space servicing is the newest infrastructure layer in the space economy. Who owns the depot, who sets the prices, and what happens when a serviced asset is damaged in the process?
Facilitator notes: Works best with unexpected persona pairings. Strong collision when persona does not belong at the depot.

Name: Commercial Orbital Station
Short description: A privately owned habitat in orbit, part hotel, part lab, part factory.
Extended description: Post-ISS commercial operators are building stations for government tenants, researchers and tourists. Multiple owners, multiple customers, one very expensive address.
Facilitator notes: The government anchor-tenant model is the key financial design question. Who pays if the government withdraws?

Name: Miners
Short description: How do they get paid when no one can check the work?
Extended description: Output hard to verify in real time. Wages may be deferred until cargo arrives at market.

Name: Farmers
Short description: Control the calories, control the power.
Extended description: Growers in sealed environments. Their failure is a settlement failure. Their success is leverage.

Name: Technicians
Short description: Most important in an emergency, paid least until then.
Extended description: Keeping life support and infrastructure running. Compensation lags importance until something breaks.

Name: Scientists
Short description: Who owns a discovery made far from any patent office?
Extended description: Multiple institutional flags often years from filing. IP timing and jurisdiction unresolved.

Name: Merchants
Short description: Supply chains stretched across the solar system.
Extended description: Margin lives in timing, route choice, and trust at both ends.

Name: Smugglers
Short description: Working around the rules or their enforcement.
Extended description: Where formal systems fail, informal ones emerge.
Facilitator notes: Read awkwardly in compliance-heavy contexts. Substitute Informal Trader if needed.

Name: Entrepreneurs
Short description: Starting ventures far from their investors.
Extended description: Capital from Earth; oversight impossible. Trust is the binding constraint.

Name: Prospectors
Short description: Gambling on a hunch, a rumour, or a sensor reading.
Extended description: High risk, high return, often years between attempts.

Name: Brokers
Short description: Information as currency.
Extended description: Trade in price discovery and reputation.

Name: Doctors
Short description: Life and death far from hospitals.
Extended description: Evacuation is impossible. Liability and decision authority both unresolved.

Name: Contractors
Short description: Portable reputation, project to project.
Extended description: Record travels with them, but verification is slow.

Name: Migrant Workers
Short description: Sending money home across distance and time.
Extended description: Remittance timing, currency and conversion are constant pressures.
Facilitator notes: Strong for cross-cultural decks.

Name: Ship Crews
Short description: Months in transit between economies.
Extended description: Paid in different jurisdictions, spending in others, banking somewhere else.

Name: Earth Investors
Short description: Cannot visit the investments.
Extended description: Reporting cadence and information lag are structural.

Name: Bankers
Short description: Local trust networks doing what banks do.
Extended description: Could be a chartered bank, a cooperative, a hawaladar, an arisan group or a DAO.
Facilitator notes: Deliberately ambiguous about banking tradition. Different rooms read this differently. That is the point.

Name: Heirs
Short description: Assets that outlived the people who owned them.
Extended description: Inheritors of contracts, claims or shares whose original holders are deceased or unreachable.

Name: Customs Officers
Short description: Controlling borders between jurisdictions.
Extended description: Mirror image of Smugglers.

Name: Children
Short description: Born in space with a different status than their parents.
Extended description: Citizenship, custody and inheritance rights cross multiple legal systems.
Facilitator notes: Born in space different status alone leaves teams worldbuilding. Give enough situation to start play.

Name: Retirees
Short description: Pensions far from issuers.
Extended description: Drawing income from systems paid into decades and millions of kilometers ago.

Name: Tourists
Short description: Brief visitors with deep pockets and shallow context.
Extended description: Big spenders, weak political constituency.

Name: Cooperative Stewards
Short description: Trusted holders of shared community resources.
Extended description: Administers a rotating savings club, mutual aid pool or community land trust.
Facilitator notes: Useful in cross-cultural decks.

Name: Protocol Designers
Short description: Architects of programmable financial systems.
Extended description: Builders of smart contracts, automated market makers, on-chain identity.
Facilitator notes: Pairs with DeFi tools. Strong for fintech-fluent rooms.

Name: Religious Endowments
Short description: Money held in trust forever, spent only on what the founder named.
Extended description: Waqf, monastery treasuries, temple foundations. Multi-generational capital with non-financial obligations.
Facilitator notes: Strong for non-Western and cross-tradition decks.

Name: Servicing Technician
Short description: Repairs and refuels assets that belong to someone else.
Extended description: The technician touches assets worth hundreds of millions under contracts whose liability terms are still being invented. Works wherever equipment exists — from near-Earth depots to probes that have not been visited in decades.
Facilitator notes: Written to work across all locations not just Near Earth. Servicing Technician at a comet claim touching a probe under a contract held by the original operator heirs is more interesting than Servicing Technician at a depot.

Name: Ground Station Operator
Short description: Runs the Earth-side link every space asset depends on.
Extended description: Whoever controls ground access controls the mission. The pricing and capacity models are evolving, and the leverage is real — even from the surface of a planet.
Facilitator notes: Earth-side persona that creates productive distance from deep space locations. Strong with Lagrange Stations, Spectrum and Orbital Slots, and Letters of Credit.

Name: Informal Trader
Short description: Working around the rules or their enforcement.
Extended description: Where formal systems fail, informal ones emerge. The same card as Smugglers without the criminal framing.
Facilitator notes: Drop-in replacement for PER-006 Smugglers in compliance-heavy or public-sector rooms. Use one or the other, never both.

Name: Loans
Short description: Funds advanced now, repaid later with interest.
Extended description: Assumes the lender can find the borrower and enforce repayment. Both break in space.

Name: Bonds
Short description: Borrowing from many lenders over years.
Extended description: Coupon payments depend on the issuer being reachable.

Name: Mortgages
Short description: Long-term loan secured by property.
Extended description: Off-Earth property requires continuous life-support spending.

Name: Shares
Short description: Partial ownership of a company. Voting rights across light-minutes.
Extended description: Voting cadence assumes shareholders can be informed and respond within reasonable time.

Name: Venture Capital
Short description: Money for a new business in exchange for owning part of it.
Extended description: Founder-investor relationship depends on frequent information exchange.

Name: Insurance
Short description: Pooled funds covering specified losses.
Extended description: Insurance assumes claims can be verified. Neither adjuster nor court scales across distance.

Name: Futures
Short description: Locking in a price now for delivery later.
Extended description: Standard maturities are months. Stretching to decades changes the math fundamentally.

Name: Derivatives
Short description: A contract whose value rides on the price of something else.
Extended description: Pricing depends on observable, verifiable inputs.
Facilitator notes: Vocabulary-heavy. Use only with finance-fluent audiences.

Name: Remittances
Short description: Sending money from worker to family across distance.
Extended description: Real systems include hawala, OFW corridors and mobile money.
Facilitator notes: Strong with informal-finance-fluent audiences.

Name: Letters of Credit
Short description: A bank guarantees payment once conditions are met.
Extended description: Invented in medieval trade to solve exactly the problem space recreates.
Facilitator notes: The Earth precedent for the whole game. Worth foregrounding when teaching.

Name: Escrow
Short description: Third party holds funds until both sides perform.
Extended description: Depends on a trusted third party. Who is that in space?

Name: Trade Credit
Short description: Buy now, pay later — extended by the seller, not a bank.
Extended description: Relies on knowing your counterparty.

Name: Savings
Short description: Value held now for use later. What interest rate when there is no central bank?
Extended description: Assumes a stable store of value and a return for waiting.

Name: Pensions
Short description: Income paid in retirement, funded by contributions over a working life.
Extended description: Inflation, currency and institutional survival are all open questions across distance.

Name: Trusts
Short description: Assets held by one party for the benefit of another across generations.
Extended description: Assumes a trustworthy trustee who outlives the grantor.

Name: Crowdfunding
Short description: Many small contributors, one project.
Extended description: Verification of the project is the binding constraint.

Name: Mutual Aid Pools
Short description: Groups covering each other's losses, without an external insurer.
Extended description: Takaful, friendly societies, rotating savings clubs. Members both fund and claim.
Facilitator notes: Bridges Western and non-Western finance.

Name: Grants
Short description: Money given without repayment, allocated by a committee.
Extended description: Who has authority to judge worthiness off-Earth?

Name: Leasing
Short description: Using something without owning it.
Extended description: Lessor needs some way to reclaim asset if payments stop.

Name: Credit Lines
Short description: Borrowing you have agreed in advance and use when you need it.
Extended description: Depends on the issuer's ability to assess and adjust risk.

Name: Parametric Insurance
Short description: Payouts triggered by measurable events, not by claims investigation.
Extended description: Pays out automatically when a defined trigger fires. Already deployed in space operations.
Facilitator notes: Strong with finance-fluent and space-industry rooms.

Name: Tokenized Equity
Short description: Ownership stakes as transferable digital tokens.
Extended description: Programmable shares. Can be split, transferred, or made conditional via smart contracts.

Name: Automated Market Makers
Short description: Algorithmic exchanges that price and clear trades without an order book.
Extended description: Removes the need for counterparty matching.

Name: Profit-Sharing Contracts
Short description: Investment that returns a share of profits rather than fixed interest.
Extended description: Mudaraba and musharaka in Islamic finance. Works where interest is forbidden.
Facilitator notes: Bridges Western VC and Islamic finance traditions.

Name: Sukuk
Short description: Asset-backed certificates compliant with Islamic finance principles.
Extended description: Holders own a share of an underlying asset and receive proceeds rather than interest.

Name: Rotating Savings Clubs
Short description: Members contribute regularly; each takes a turn receiving the pot.
Extended description: Arisan, hui, susu, tanda — ROSCAs. Works on social trust without formal banking.
Facilitator notes: Important for cross-cultural decks.

Name: Reputation Systems
Short description: Your record of keeping promises, treated as something you own.
Extended description: Stands in for enforcement when there are no courts. Can be traded, or put at risk to back a promise.

Name: Prediction Markets
Short description: Trading contracts that pay out based on real-world outcomes.
Extended description: Useful for verification when no central authority can confirm an outcome.

Name: Waqf
Short description: A permanent endowment whose income funds a public purpose.
Extended description: The principal is preserved and never spent; only the income is used. Multi-century time horizons. Foundational institution in Islamic finance.

Name: Programmable Escrow
Short description: Software holds the money and releases it when the conditions are met.
Extended description: No third party holds the money. The code does, and the code decides when it moves.
Facilitator notes: Pairs with Letters of Credit as a comparison point.

Name: Auctions
Short description: How do you set a price when nothing like it has ever been sold?
Extended description: How do you price the first asteroid ore at market? English auctions reward patience; Dutch auctions (invented for perishable goods that could not wait) reward speed. Sealed bids handle claims where revealing your valuation is dangerous.
Facilitator notes: Dutch auction variant particularly relevant for time-sensitive space cargo. Strong for any combination involving first extraction or novel assets.

Name: Freeports
Short description: Duty-free zones where goods sit outside every surrounding jurisdiction.
Extended description: Freeports exist because of jurisdictional arbitrage — the value of being between legal systems rather than inside one. Not a location but a legal and financial structure that can be applied to a location. The question of which jurisdiction rules apply at a Lagrange Station, orbital waypoint or transit hub is exactly the freeport problem.
Facilitator notes: Pairs naturally with Earth Spaceports and Lagrange Stations. Also connects to the colonial history — freeports were instruments of extraction logic letting trading companies move goods across jurisdictions without declaring value.

Name: Launch Contracts
Short description: Buying a slot on a rocket years before it flies at a price negotiated today.
Extended description: Long lead times, limited cancellation rights, and a secondary market that did not exist a decade ago. The contract structure invented for expendable rockets is being renegotiated for a reusable world.
Facilitator notes: Pairs naturally with Earth Spaceports and Commercial Orbital Station.

Name: Spectrum and Orbital Slots
Short description: An invisible, finite claim on a frequency and a position in orbit.
Extended description: Orbital slots and radio frequencies are allocated by international treaty. They can be held, sub-licensed, and in some cases traded. How do you borrow against an asset you cannot touch that expires if unused, and that a treaty revision could make worthless overnight?
Facilitator notes: The secondary market for spectrum is real. The question of what backs the value and what could destroy it is the productive collision point.
